## Parent

Epic `77e3-28e2-31ec-47ec`. This is the net-mechanism half of deliverable 3 — the RED
PROOF for the `project.net-mechanism` criterion created by `fe94-2e22-ea9e-46f7`.

Split from `fe94` because carrying the criterion and its corpus in one description exceeds
the 8,000-character plan-review admission cap `verify.max_ticket_description_chars`
(measured: 15,612 characters combined, against an unconfigured schema default of 8,000 at
`src/rebar/_config_schema.py:52`).

## Why firing proof cannot live in a unit test

Measured from the sibling criterion's test module: `tests/unit/test_project_portability_criterion.py`
never executes model judgment. It asserts activation, routing metadata, front-matter keys,
prompt resolution, and the presence of required headings in the rubric body — all
structural. A unit test asserting "this plan is scored as a finding" could only do so
against a canned score, which proves the fixture and not the criterion.

So `fe94` carries only structural tests, and ALL firing behaviour is proven here, in the
calibration corpus — the same place `project.portability` proves its own.

## The corpus

`.rebar/evals/plan-review-project-net-mechanism.eval.yaml`, modeled on
`.rebar/evals/plan-review-project-portability.eval.yaml` (215 lines, read from the working
tree). Config: a top-level `prompt: plan-review-project-net-mechanism` key selecting the
criterion (the portability spec's own top-level selector), `epochs: 3`,
`gate: at_least(2)`, `coverage_threshold: 1.0`, and a deterministic
`emits_valid_findings` scorer. Case labels use the loader's vocabulary —
`expect: finding` for fire and `expect: pass` for no-fire
(`src/rebar/llm/evals/eval_scorers.py:32-33`); `fire`/`no-fire` are not in
`ALLOWED_EXPECTS` and would score every case non-applicable. Dataset is BALANCED — 4 must-fire and 4
must-not-fire cases, each carrying `id`, `corpus`, `criterion`, `expect`, `note`, `input`.

The spec also carries a `gold_set`, as the portability referent does at
`.rebar/evals/plan-review-project-portability.eval.yaml:199-215`: 8 one-line
`input`/`label` entries, 4 labeled `finding` and 4 labeled `pass`. This is not optional
decoration — `src/rebar/llm/evals/eval.py:265-267` appends
"strict: eval spec needs a non-empty `gold_set` (judge kappa alignment)" when it is
absent, so without one the spec fails strict validation before any case is scored, and
the sibling assertion `validate_eval_spec(spec) == []`
(`tests/unit/test_project_portability_eval.py:53`) could not pass. The gold_set aligns the
judge; the dataset scores the criterion.

Balance is the point: a corpus of only must-fire cases cannot distinguish a working
criterion from one that fires on everything.

### Must-fire

- `NETMECH-F1` — the red-proof case, below.
- `NETMECH-F2` — adds a `feature_flag`, gives a reason, names no retirement.
- `NETMECH-F3` — adds an `autouse_fixture`, framed as "small enough not to count".
- `NETMECH-F4` — adds a `ci_gate` and a `config_key`, retires neither.

### Must-not-fire

- `NETMECH-N1` — adds an `env_var` and names the `config_key` it retires.
- `NETMECH-N2` — adds a `lock` and states why no retirement is possible.
- `NETMECH-N3` — adds no mechanism of any of the seven kinds.
- `NETMECH-N4` — only removes mechanisms.

`N1` and `N2` exist because the criterion's threshold has two independent escape conditions
(a named retirement, or a stated justification); a corpus exercising only one would leave
the other unproven.

## The red-proof referent

`NETMECH-F1` derives from a change that actually landed. `2041-75d6-2a2f-4be9` added the
`env_var` `REBAR_LLM_EMBEDDING_MODEL`, admitted by the marker at
`src/rebar/llm/config_readers.py:152`; the name is consequently ABSENT from
`.github/mechanism-baseline.json`, because the marker admits it so it never enters the
baseline. Nothing was retired alongside it. Both facts were verified directly.

Stated precisely so the case is not mistaken for a quotation: `2041`'s plan TEXT was not
read. What was measured is the landed OUTCOME — a mechanism added, admitted by marker, no
retirement recorded. `F1`'s `input` is a faithful reconstruction of that outcome as plan
prose, not an excerpt of `2041`, and `F1`'s `note` records that distinction along with the
marker line as its provenance.

This is what makes the corpus a red proof rather than a self-fulfilling test: the case is
drawn from a change the existing ratchet passed and this criterion should have caught.

## Files this change touches

1. `.rebar/evals/plan-review-project-net-mechanism.eval.yaml` — NEW, the corpus.
2. `tests/unit/test_project_net_mechanism_eval.py` — NEW, offline shape checks on the
   spec, modeled on the portability eval test. Runs no model.

## Portability and provider neutrality

The offline shape checks parse YAML and assert structure; they touch no network, no CI
environment, and no provider. They pass with no CI provider configured and with no model
API key present.

The eval spec's `model` key names the model the corpus was CALIBRATED against. It does not
constrain which provider or model runs the criterion in production — routing selects that
independently — so this corpus does not narrow rebar's provider support.

## Acceptance criteria

Each names one deliverable; none bundles two with "and".

Offline, in `tests/unit/test_project_net_mechanism_eval.py`:

- [x] The spec parses as YAML.
- [x] The spec declares `prompt: plan-review-project-net-mechanism`.
- [x] The dataset contains exactly 4 cases with `expect: finding`.
- [x] The dataset contains exactly 4 cases with `expect: pass`.
- [x] Every case carries all six of `id`, `corpus`, `criterion`, `expect`, `note`, `input`.
- [x] Every case `id` is unique.
- [x] The spec declares `epochs: 3`.
- [x] The spec declares `gate: at_least(2)`.
- [x] The spec declares `coverage_threshold: 1.0`.
- [x] The spec declares a `gold_set` of exactly 8 entries, 4 labeled `finding` and 4
      labeled `pass`, each with a nonempty `input` and `label`.
- [x] `validate_eval_spec(spec)` returns an empty list, so the spec passes strict
      validation.
- [x] `NETMECH-F1`'s `note` cites `src/rebar/llm/config_readers.py:152`.
- [x] The test module executes no model call, asserted by the module importing no runner.

Semantic, operator-attested rather than a test:

- [x] `rebar criteria eval project.net-mechanism --runs 3` meets the declared gate on all
      8 cases, with the run output recorded as a comment on this ticket.

Gate:

- [x] `make verify` exits 0.

## Dependency

Depends on `fe94-2e22-ea9e-46f7`: the rubric must exist before the corpus can be evaluated
against it. Recorded as a `depends_on` link, so `ready` will not surface this ticket until
`fe94` closes.
